approach: B: restore-dual-write (re-add SyncDispositionToClickhouse dispatch). NOTE: approach pivoted 2026-07-09 — the earlier 'repoint-reads-to-cdc' (Approach A) was implemented + 3-lane-reviewed, then REVERTED after review+live-prod-perf showed it carried a ~3.7s/query regression on a 3.5B-row table, missed 2 raw-SQL heatmap queries, and had tombstone/empty-string edges. Dalton chose the simpler uniform fix: restore the dual-write so all read surfaces work unchanged.
synthesis: Setting a validation disposition on a scan in the Missed Opportunity dashboard (and, by the same latent bug, the ClickHouse-backed Hits and Scans lists) does not update the 'Validation' column or drop the item from the default queue. Root cause: those three surfaces read a flat `disposition` column on the wide ClickHouse tables (clarity.missed_opportunities, hits_hot/hits_cold, scans_hot/scans_cold) that stopped being written on 2026-04-14 when the SyncDispositionToClickhouse dispatch was removed from Scan::updateDisposition (commit 1b241ae1). Per the ticket owner, that flat column is being DEPRECATED — the fix is NOT to restore the job but to REPOINT the disposition reads (both the DEV-2033 default-view exclude/include filter AND the displayed value) onto the live PeerDB CDC mirror zod.scans_metadata_extracted (fresh disposition Nullable(String), keyed by scan_id), for all three surfaces. The Postgres write path (Scan::updateDisposition writes scans_metadata.meta, which CDC-syncs onward) is already correct and unchanged. No production backfill — repointed reads use the fresh source, so already-stuck hits resolve automatically. The Postgres-backed branches of Hits/Scans already read fresh data (direct scans_metadata join) and are unaffected; only the CH branches are broken.

scope.summary: Repoint the disposition READS for the 3 ClickHouse-backed list surfaces (Missed Opportunity, Hits, Scans) off the orphaned flat CH `disposition` column onto zod.scans_metadata_extracted. Two decoupled, no-JOIN mechanisms: (a) filter side — rewrite the disposition scopes on the CH MissedOpportunity/Hit/Scan models to use a kit-scoped, argMax-deduped NOT-IN/IN subquery against scans_metadata_extracted; (b) display side — per-page point-lookup hydration of $record->disposition in each page's paginateTableQuery(). Add a ScansMetadataExtracted CH model + factory. Add/adapt regression tests for all three surfaces. No write-path change, no backfill.

questions.q: Was removing the SyncDispositionToClickhouse dispatch in commit 1b241ae1 ('rely on PG entirely') an intentional migration toward Postgres/CDC as the disposition source, or an accidental removal to simply revert?
questions.answer: INTENTIONAL migration. The flat CH `disposition` column on the wide tables is being deprecated; the correct fix is to repoint the MO/Hits/Scans disposition READS onto the live Postgres-backed source (PeerDB CDC mirror zod.scans_metadata_extracted / view clarity.scans_metadata, which already keeps disposition fresh), NOT to restore the orphaned ALTER-UPDATE job. Do not re-add the dispatch.

questions.q: Should this ticket include a one-off backfill of ClickHouse `disposition` for scans dispositioned during the outage window, or split it out?
questions.answer: NO backfill. With reads repointed to the live CDC/PG disposition source there is no stale flat CH column to backfill — already-affected hits resolve automatically once reads use the fresh source.

questions.q: Should the fix/tests/QA explicitly cover the Hits list and the ClickHouse-backed Scans list too, or keep the PR MO-scoped?
questions.answer: COVER ALL THREE explicitly — Missed Opportunity + Hits + Scans. All three read the same orphaned flat column and must be repointed; tests/QA must prove all three un-break.

notes: zod.scans_metadata_extracted (clickhouse-schema.sql:79): scan_id Int64, kit_id Nullable(Int32), disposition Nullable(String), _peerdb_version, _peerdb_is_deleted; ENGINE ReplacingMergeTree(_peerdb_version,_peerdb_is_deleted) ORDER BY scan_id; idx_disposition set(20) but NO kit_id index. Dedup via argMax(_,_peerdb_version) — do NOT use FINAL on zod CDC tables.

No JOIN anywhere: every CH Eloquent model in app/Clickhouse/Models uses whereIntegerInRaw/whereRaw subqueries, zero ->join() — the custom Clickhouse builder's join compilation is unexercised. Filter = IN/NOT-IN subquery; display = per-page point lookup (ClickHouse has no correlated subqueries).

CRITICAL NULL-safety: express exclusion as NOT-IN over the EXCLUDED set, never IN over the passing set. Scans with zero metadata rows (never synced) or current NULL disposition are absent from any 'disposition = X' subquery; NOT-IN keeps them visible (correct: Awaiting Review), an IN-passing-set would drop them. The write path only ever writes a value, never NULL, so 'no row yet' is the common steady state for undispositioned scans.
Query zod.scans_metadata_extracted DIRECTLY (kit-scoped), not via the clarity.scans_metadata view (which pre-filters org type=1 with unclear semantics and is un-deduped).

CDC lag: PG write -> PeerDB CDC -> scans_metadata_extracted is the same pipeline other consumers use (seconds to low-single-digit minutes). Owner accepted this as the tradeoff for deprecating the flat column; it is a strict improvement over 'never updates' (permanently stale since 2026-04-14).
DEV-2033's scopeExcludeDisposition semantics (Awaiting-Review/NULL stays in default view; Invalid excluded) must be preserved exactly through the repoint.
Root cause / approach corroborated: fast-pass prep + adversarial verifier (confidence 88) + grep backstop (0 missed callers) + design pass (confidence 75, limited only by unverified prod-scale perf).
